title: Wren and the Homecoming
premise: At Ashgrove Academy, Casper Blackwood has survived three years on a scholarship by being unremarkable—until the senior college essay prompt asks students to write about a truth they've never told. Casper's truth is explosive: the beloved founder's legacy her best friend Priya's family is about to inherit is built on a lie Casper alone can prove, because the evidence lives in her late mother's letters. Telling it means losing Priya, betraying the scholarship patrons who saved her, and facing the academy's machinery of quiet intimidation. Casper publishes the essay anyway, and in the wreckage of prom night she discovers that the friend worth losing is the friend worth fighting to win back—and that inheritance, rightly understood, is something you claim rather than receive.
about_author: Xanthe Crane is a former boarding-school librarian who spent a decade cataloging other people's secrets before writing her own. She lives in a drafty farmhouse in Vermont with two cats named after minor Romantic poets.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Unremarkable
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Opening week of senior year at Ashgrove Academy; Casper narrates her survival rules of invisibility while tutoring wealthy classmates and dodging attention. Emotional beat: weary contentment that the reader will immediately sense is fragile.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper and her best friend Priya Whitmore, heir to the Ashgrove founding family, share their ritual Friday diner nights. Priya announces the family is being honored with a legacy gala and a new scholarship wing in her grandmother's name. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by Casper's flicker of guilt.

chapters.title: The Question on the Board
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. College counselor Ms. Okafor assigns the common app essay: 'Write about a truth you have never told.' Casper freezes, because she has one, large and buried. Emotional beat: the first crack in her armor, dread disguised as writer's block.

chapters.title: Letters in the Attic
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Home for fall break, Casper rereads her late mother's letters from her own Ashgrove days and finds references to a falsified donation record tied to the Whitmore founding myth. Emotional beat: grief curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: What Priya Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya prepares for the gala, terrified she'll fail her grandmother's memory, and confesses to Casper that she feels like a fraud. Casper almost tells her everything—and doesn't. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Draft One, Burned
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper writes the essay honestly, then deletes it, then prints it and hides it. Ms. Okafor notices her paralysis and gently pushes: 'The essay that costs you something is the only one worth reading.' Emotional beat: temptation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Patron's Tea
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Headmaster Voss invites Casper to tea with the scholarship patrons, praising her discretion and hinting that her renewal depends on 'not making waves.' Casper understands she is being warned without being told anything. Emotional beat: claustrophobia—the academy is watching.

chapters.title: Archive Card 114
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper sneaks into the school archive and confirms her mother's letters match a gap in the founding records: the endowment that built Ashgrove's name was quietly taken from a dismissed Black employee, her great-aunt. Emotional beat: the truth becomes undeniable, and so does her kinship to it.

chapters.title: Half-Truths at the Gala
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the Whitmore legacy gala, Casper watches Priya give a speech about her grandmother's 'generosity' and nearly objects aloud; instead she lies to Priya's face about being fine. Emotional beat: guilt as betrayal, the friendship straining under Casper's silence.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Saw Her
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Theo, a day student who works in the archive, reveals he noticed her research and offers help—and maybe more. Casper, unused to being seen, panics and pushes him away. Emotional beat: fear of visibility in love as in truth.

chapters.title: Voss's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Headmaster Voss offers Casper a full-ride to her dream college, arranged by the patrons—contingent, unmistakably, on her 'continued good judgment.' Emotional beat: the bribe that makes silence feel like complicity.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Is For
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers Casper has been meeting Theo and researching her family, and feels betrayed by the secrecy. She confronts Casper; Casper can't explain without detonating everything. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Cold Shoulder Season
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The friendship freezes; Priya sits with new friends, the diner booth empty. Casper throws herself into finishing the essay, alone. Emotional beat: loneliness as both punishment and clarity.

chapters.title: Aunt Delia's Name
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper tracks down Delia Black's surviving descendants and learns the family was paid off, silenced, and erased from the school's story. One descendant gives Casper a photograph to use 'if she's brave enough.' Emotional beat: inheritance reframed—she is the inheritor after all.

chapters.title: Submission
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper submits the true essay to Ms. Okafor and, at Theo's suggestion, to the school paper's anonymous tip line. Her hands shake; she feels lighter and doomed at once. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Story Breaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The paper publishes the archive findings with Casper's essay appended. The school erupts; Voss suspends the paper, patrons threaten Casper's funding, and Priya learns the truth from a headline instead of her best friend. Emotional beat: the cost arrives all at once.

chapters.title: Prom Is Cancelled, Then It Isn't
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. In the fallout, the gala and prom are 'postponed indefinitely.' Priya, humiliated and furious, finally reads Casper's essay itself—and recognizes her mother's handwriting in the letters quoted. Emotional beat: anger cracking into understanding.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Voss convenes a disciplinary hearing to expel Casper for 'misuse of archives.' Priya walks in uninvited and testifies that the archive was open to students and the truth was owed to everyone. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing truth—the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: What the Whitmores Owe
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts her parents, who knew and chose silence; she announces she will not accept an inheritance built on Delia Black's erasure unless it's renamed and repaired. Emotional beat: Priya claims her own inheritance—conscience.

chapters.title: The Essay That Got In
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Acceptance letters arrive; the dream college admits her on the strength of the essay Voss tried to bury, no patron money required. Ms. Okafor tells her the truth cost exactly what it was worth. Emotional beat: vindication without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Prom, Uninvited
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Priya, as student council president, reinstates prom with a new name: the Delia Black Memorial Dance. She asks Casper to come—not as a friend yet, but as a start. Casper wears her mother's dress. Emotional beat: tentative forgiveness, love outlasting duty.

chapters.title: Wren at the Window
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, epilogue. Graduation: the wing is renamed, Delia's photograph hangs in the archive, and Priya saves her a seat. Casper reflects that she stopped being invisible the moment she told the truth—and that being seen was the homecoming all along. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
